mainTopic: Round windows and the קיסרי measuring rule, רב נחמן on high windows and ceiling openings in houses, and the new משנה about a wall between two courtyards.
overview: The amud opens by explaining רבי יוחנן's rule that a round חלון needs a circumference of 24 טפחים so that a 4×4 square fits inside it. The גמרא challenges this twice with geometry. The quarter rule suggests 16, and the diagonal rule (1 side gives 1⅖ diagonal) suggests 17 minus ⅕. It answers that רבי יוחנן followed the scholars of קיסרי: a circle around a square is bigger by half, so 16 plus 8 gives 24. Next, רב נחמן rules that the 10-טפחים height limit applies only to a window between courtyards. A window between houses works even when high, because a house is treated as full. רבא challenges him from a ברייתא, and the גמרא defends רב נחמן by saying the ברייתא's 'all the same' refers only to the 4×4 size. רב נחמן then rules that a ceiling opening from a house to an attic needs no ladder at all, neither permanent nor temporary. A new משנה follows about a wall between two courtyards: when it is intact, when it has produce on top, and when it is breached up to or beyond ten אמות. The גמרא begins by asking about a wall less than four טפחים wide. רב answers that both domains control it, so nothing may be moved on it.

steps.title: The 12-handbreadth rule only describes a circle, not a square inside it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן needs more than 12 טפחים. The 3-to-1 ratio describes the circle itself, but a square placed inside the circle needs a bigger circle.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies to a circle, but for a square we need more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the earlier question of why רבי יוחנן needs 24 טפחים when a circle 4 across measures only 12 around. It says the 12 is correct for the circle alone, but a 4×4 square must fit inside, and that needs a larger circle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A circle with a 4-טפחים width has a circumference of about 12 (width × 3). A 4×4 square is wider at its corners than 4, so it does not fit inside that circle. The window therefore has to be bigger than 12 around, and the גמרא now has to work out by how much.

keyTerms.meaning: These words / this rule applies (only to a specific case)

steps.confusionAlert: The halachic requirement is a 4×4 square opening. The question is never how big the circle is by itself. It is how big the circle must be so that the whole square fits inside it.

phrases.english: These words (the 3-to-1 ratio giving 12) apply to a circle,
but for a square (that must fit inside it), we require more.
phrases.notes: The square's corners stick out past 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּעִיגּוּלָא, אֲבָל בְּרִיבּוּעָא בָּעִינַן טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier: why 24 and not 12?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between measuring a circle and fitting a square inside a circle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A circle 12 around, being 4 across, should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The square's corners stick out past 4, so a larger circle is needed.

steps.title: A square is only a quarter bigger than a circle, so 16 should be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using the known rule that a square exceeds a circle by a quarter. By that rule, a circle of 16 טפחים should suffice, not 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, how much is a square larger than a circle? A quarter. So sixteen should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that more than 12 is needed but asks why it should be as much as 24. Since a square is only a quarter bigger than a circle, 16 should be the most that is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A circle 4 across is 12 around, and a 4×4 square drawn around it is 16 around. That is 4 more, a quarter of the square's 16. The גמרא concludes that a circle of 16 should be large enough, which makes רבי יוחנן's 24 look exaggerated.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (opens a logical challenge from known facts)

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי, כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יָתֵר עַל הֶעָגוֹל —
phrases.english: Now, by how much is a square larger than a circle?
phrases.notes: Opens with a known geometric rule.

phrases.english: By a quarter. So with sixteen it should suffice!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, כַּמָּה מְרוּבָּע יָתֵר עַל הֶעָגוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how much 'more' Step 1 requires.
steps.kashyaTarget: The size of 24 טפחים required by רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the quarter rule, the needed circle is at most 16, so 24 is too large.

steps.title: The quarter rule is for a circle inside a square, not a square inside a circle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the quarter rule applies when a circle sits inside a square. When a square must sit inside a circle, more is needed because of the corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to a circle that sits inside a square. But a square that sits inside a circle needs more. Why? Because of the sticking-out corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out that the quarter rule describes the wrong situation. Here the square goes inside the circle, and that requires a larger circle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a circle sits inside a square, the circle touches the middle of each side, and the difference is a quarter. When a square sits inside a circle, the circle must reach the square's corners, which are farther from the center than its sides. So the circle has to be bigger than 16.

keyTerms.meaning: That comes out from within (inscribed inside)
The projection (sticking out) of the corners

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pictures. A circle inside a square needs the smaller difference (a quarter). A square inside a circle needs the larger difference because of the corners.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי עִיגּוּלָא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ רִיבּוּעָא.
phrases.english: These words apply to a circle that comes out from within a square (inscribed in it).
phrases.notes: Circle inside square, so the quarter rule works.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל רִיבּוּעָא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ עִיגּוּלָא, בָּעִינַן טְפֵי.
phrases.english: But a square that comes out from within a circle requires more.
phrases.notes: Our case: the square inside the round window.

phrases.english: What is the reason? Because of the projection of the corners.
phrases.notes: The corners are farther from the center than the sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי עִיגּוּלָא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ רִיבּוּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: inscribed circle versus inscribed square.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The quarter rule caps the requirement at 16.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a square inside a circle, the corners demand a larger circle than 16.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the next challenge: if the corners determine the size, we need to calculate exactly how far they stick out.

steps.title: Using the diagonal, 17 minus a fifth should be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again using the diagonal rule: each אמה of a square's side gives 1⅖ on the diagonal. That makes the needed circle about 16⅘ טפחים, still far less than 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, every אמה of a square is an אמה and two-fifths on the diagonal. So seventeen minus a fifth should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the corners matter and calculates exactly how big the circle must be. The result is still well below רבי יוחנן's 24, so the challenge comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 4×4 square has an אלכסון of 4 × 1⅖ = 5⅗ טפחים. A circle passing through the corners must be 5⅗ across. Multiplying by 3 gives 16⅘ around, which is 17 minus a fifth, so why does רבי יוחנן need 24?

keyTerms.meaning: An אמה (cubit); here the unit of a side

steps.whatToRemember: The math gives 12 for the circle alone, at most 16 by the quarter rule, and 16⅘ using the diagonal. None of these reaches רבי יוחנן's 24, so the גמרא still has to explain his number. The next step (Step 5) does this.

phrases.english: Now, since every cubit (of side) in a square
is a cubit and two-fifths on the diagonal,
then seventeen minus a fifth should suffice!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, כׇּל אַמְּתָא בְּרִיבּוּעַ אַמְּתָא וּתְרֵי חוּמְּשֵׁי בַּאֲלַכְסוֹנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts Step 3's point about the corners, then measures them precisely to challenge again.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An exact diagonal calculation gives a needed circumference of 16⅘, so 24 is far more than necessary.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן Followed the Scholars of קיסרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the diagonal challenge. רבי יוחנן used the rule of the judges or scholars of קיסרי: a circle inside a square is smaller by a quarter, and a circle around a square is bigger by half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן spoke like the judges of קיסרי, and some say like the sages of קיסרי, who say: a circle inside a square is smaller by a quarter, and a circle around a square is bigger by half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge. רבי יוחנן was following a different, more generous measuring rule from the scholars of קיסרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 4x4 square has a perimeter of 16 טפחים. By the קיסרי rule, the circle that goes around it must be bigger by half of 16, which is 8. That gives 24 טפחים, exactly רבי יוחנן's number.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages of Caesarea (an alternate version of who said it)

steps.whatToRemember: 24 טפחים comes from the קיסרי rule: start with the square's 16-טפחים perimeter and add half (8), giving 24.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. When the circle is inside the square, the difference is a quarter. When the square is inside the circle, the difference is half. רבי יוחנן's case is the second one.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר כִּי דַּיָּינֵי דְקֵיסָרִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan spoke like the judges of Caesarea,
and some say: like the Sages of Caesarea,
phrases.notes: Two versions of who taught the rule

phrases.english: who say: a circle inside a square is smaller by a quarter,
a square inside a circle: the difference is half.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר כִּי דַּיָּינֵי דְקֵיסָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the diagonal-rule challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different authoritative measuring rule that רבי יוחנן relied on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exact diagonal geometry gives only about 16⅘, so 24 seems far too much
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן used the קיסרי rule that a circle around a square is bigger by half, giving 24

steps.title: רב נחמן: A High Window Between Houses Still Works
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the משנה's 10-טפחים height requirement applies only to a window between courtyards. Between two houses, even a high window lets them make one עירוב, because a house is treated as if it were full.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'less than four by four, etc.' רב נחמן said: they taught this only about a window between two courtyards. But a window between two houses, even above ten, works too. If they want to make one עירוב, they may. Why? A house is viewed as if it were full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. רב נחמן limits the 10-טפחים height rule to courtyards only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a courtyard, a high window is far from the ground and not easy to use. A house, however, is treated as if it were filled up to its windows. So a window in a house never counts as 'too high,' and only the courtyard needs the 10-טפחים limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Above ten טפחים from the ground
Considered as if it is full

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of this passage. The coming challenge and answers all test whether רב נחמן's house-versus-courtyard distinction holds up.

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] 'Less than four by four, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quote of the next line of the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: they only taught this
about a window between two courtyards,
but a window between two houses,
even if it is above ten as well,
if they want to make an עירוב, they make one עירוב.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא? בֵּיתָא כְּמַאן דִּמְלֵי דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: What is the reason? A house is considered as if it is full.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 10-טפחים height limit applies only to courtyards. Between houses, a window above 10 still allows one עירוב, because a house is viewed as full.

steps.title: רבא Challenges רב נחמן From a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא that lists windows between courtyards, houses, attics, roofs and rooms. It says all are the same: 4x4 and within 10 טפחים. This seems to contradict רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: 'A window between two courtyards, between two houses, between two attics, between two roofs, and between two rooms are all the same to me. All must be four by four and within ten!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling with a ברייתא that seems to require the 10-טפחים limit even for houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explicitly includes 'two houses' in its list. It then says every case needs the window within ten. That directly clashes with רב נחמן's claim that a high window between houses is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source)
They are all the same to me
Within ten טפחים of the ground

phrases.english: Rava challenged Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד לִי חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת,
phrases.english: 'All the same to me are a window between two courtyards,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד לִי חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי בָתִּים,
phrases.english: and a window between two houses,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד לִי חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲלִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: and a window between two attics,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד לִי חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי גַגִּין,
phrases.english: and a window between two roofs,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד לִי חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי חֲדָרִים —
phrases.english: and a window between two rooms:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה בְּתוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה!
phrases.english: all must be four by four, within ten!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that a window between houses works even above 10 טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists houses together with courtyards and requires all of them to be within ten.

steps.title: The 10-טפחים Rule Refers Only to Courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's 'within ten' applies only to the courtyards in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain it as referring to courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן by reading the ברייתא's 'within ten' as aimed only at courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the houses, attics and other places in the list share the 4x4 rule. Only courtyards also need the window within ten. That matches רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it as / interpret it as referring to

phrases.english: Explain it as referring to courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגּוּמָא אַחֲצֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits part of the ברייתא's ruling to one item in the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Within ten' applies to every window in the list, including houses

steps.title: But the ברייתא Says 'All the Same'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the last answer. The ברייתא repeats 'all the same to me,' which shows that every case follows the same rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'all the same to me'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 8. The ברייתא's wording seems to make all the windows equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ten-טפחים rule were only for courtyards, the cases would not really be 'the same.' So limiting it to courtyards seems to go against the ברייתא's own words.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'all the same to me'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״אֶחָד לִי״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'within ten' applies only to courtyards
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'all the same to me' implies that all the cases share the same rules.

steps.title: 'All the Same' Refers Only to the 4x4 Size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'all the same to me' refers only to the 4x4 size requirement, not to the 10-טפחים height.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain it as referring to 'four by four.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final defense of רב נחמן. The cases are 'the same' only in needing a 4x4 window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every window in the list must be at least 4x4. The 'within ten' part is not included in 'all the same,' so a high window between houses can still work, just as רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: Four by four טפחים (the minimum window size)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן stands. All windows need to be 4x4, but only a courtyard window must also be within 10 טפחים, since a house is viewed as full.

phrases.english: Explain it as referring to 'four by four.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגּוּמָא אַאַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 9 and completes the defense of רב נחמן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what 'all the same' refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All the same' means every rule in the ברייתא applies to every window
steps.terutzMaskana: 'All the same' refers only to the 4x4 size; the 10-טפחים limit is for courtyards

steps.title: רבי אבא asks whether a ceiling opening needs a permanent ladder
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רב נחמן whether a לול (an opening from a house up to an עליה) needs a permanent ladder before the two can be joined for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא asked רב נחמן: An opening that leads from a house up to an attic. Does it need a permanent ladder to make it permitted, or does it not need a permanent ladder to make it permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא asks רב נחמן a new practical question. It is about an opening in the ceiling of a house that leads up to an attic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, an opening up high is only usable if there is a fixed way to climb to it, such as a permanent ladder. רבי אבא wants to know whether this ceiling opening also needs a permanent ladder before the house and the attic can make one עירוב together. He asks רב נחמן because רב נחמן is the one who said 'a house is treated as full' (Step 6).

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, not an attack)
An opening in the ceiling leading to the floor above
To make it permitted (to carry between them)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba asked of Rav Nachman:
An opening that opens from a house to an attic,
phrases.notes: The opening is in the ceiling of the lower house. A different person lives in the attic above.

phrases.english: does it need a permanent ladder to permit it

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין צָרִיךְ סוּלָּם קָבוּעַ לְהַתִּירוֹ?
phrases.english: or does it not need a permanent ladder to permit it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the courtyard and house windows of Steps 6-10 to a new case: an opening in a ceiling between a house and an attic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a ceiling opening between a house and an attic needs a permanent ladder before they can make one עירוב.

steps.title: Explaining the two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what the question really depends on. Does 'a house is treated as full' work only for a window in a side wall, or also for an opening in the middle of the ceiling?
steps.simpleTranslation: When we say a house is treated as if it were full, does that apply only to an opening on the side, but not to one in the middle? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain why רבי אבא was unsure. It shows the two possible ways to understand רב נחמן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said a house is treated as if it were filled up, so even a high window counts as reachable. Side 1: this works only for a window in a side wall, where the 'filled' part of the house reaches right up to it. If so, an opening in the middle of the ceiling still needs a ladder. Side 2: there is no difference, and the 'full house' idea covers the ceiling opening too, so no ladder is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is treated as if it were full
On the side (in a side wall)
Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמְרִינַן בֵּיתָא כְּמַאן דִּמְלֵי דָּמֵי —
phrases.english: When we say a house is considered as if it were full —
phrases.notes: This refers to רב נחמן's rule from Step 6.

phrases.english: does that apply only to an opening on the side,
but in the middle — not,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמְרִינַן בֵּיתָא כְּמַאן דִּמְלֵי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אבא's question in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'house is treated as full' rule is limited to side windows or also covers openings in the middle of the ceiling.

steps.title: רב נחמן answers that no ladder is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the opening does not need a ladder.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבי אבא's question with a short reply: it is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This means the 'full house' rule applies to an opening in the middle of the ceiling too. But his answer is very short. Does it mean only that a permanent ladder is not needed, or that no ladder at all is needed? The next step deals with exactly that.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Steps 11-12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A permanent ladder is not required, so the 'full house' idea also covers a ceiling opening in the middle.

steps.title: Some understood that a temporary ladder is still needed
steps.stepSummary: People concluded from רב נחמן's answer that only a permanent ladder is unnecessary, but a temporary ladder is still required.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: it is a permanent ladder that is not needed, but a temporary ladder is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how some people read רב נחמן's short answer. This is setting up the correction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the question asked about a 'permanent ladder,' they took 'it is not needed' to mean only that a permanent ladder is not needed. That would mean at least a temporary ladder must be placed there.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (an assumption that is often corrected)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is NOT the final הלכה. It is a mistaken reading that the very next step corrects.

phrases.english: They understood from it:
it is a permanent ladder that is not needed,
but a temporary ladder — is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר מִינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a narrow inference from the wording of רב נחמן's answer in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The assumed reading: a temporary ladder is still required, only a permanent one is not.

steps.title: Correction: no ladder of any kind is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר מניומי reports in רב נחמן's name that neither a permanent nor a temporary ladder is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: Both a permanent ladder and a temporary ladder — it is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a direct report of רב נחמן's view. It rejects the mistaken reading from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's real position is that no ladder at all is needed. Because the opening is inside the house, and the house is treated as full, the opening already counts as usable. That is enough for the house and the attic to make one עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an earlier teaching that was passed down)
Both this and that (the same rule for both)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a ceiling opening between a house and an attic needs no ladder at all, neither permanent nor temporary. The 'house is treated as full' rule covers an opening in the middle of the ceiling as well.

phrases.english: It was stated,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Manyumi said that Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד סוּלָּם קָבוּעַ וְאֶחָד סוּלָּם עֲרַאי —
phrases.english: both a permanent ladder and a temporary ladder —
it is not needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of Step 14 with a direct report of רב נחמן's words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that a temporary ladder is still required.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference read too much into the short answer. רב נחמן actually meant that no ladder at all is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No ladder of any kind is needed for a ceiling opening between a house and an attic.

steps.title: New משנה: a wall between two courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a wall between two courtyards is 10 טפחים high and 4 טפחים wide, the courtyards make two separate עירובין, not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A wall between two courtyards that is ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide: they make two עירובין, and they do not make one עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses a solid wall, not a window, standing between two courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall 10 טפחים high fully separates the two courtyards, and there is no opening for them to join through. So each courtyard makes its own עירוב, and they cannot join together into one עירוב. The 4-טפחים width matters for the next ruling, about using the top of the wall, and the גמרא later asks what happens when the wall is narrower (Step 19).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

phrases.english: MISHNAH
A wall that is between two courtyards,
ten handbreadths high and four wide —
they make two עירובין, and they do not make one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כּוֹתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה. The topic shifts from windows and openings to a wall between courtyards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall 10 טפחים high and 4 טפחים wide between two courtyards means they must make two separate עירובין.

steps.title: Produce on top of the dividing wall
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that residents of both courtyards may climb the wall and eat produce on top of it, but may not bring it down into a courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was produce on top of the wall, the people of this courtyard may climb up from their side and eat, and the people of that courtyard may climb up from their side and eat, as long as they do not bring the produce down.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its case of the 10-טפחים-high, 4-טפחים-wide wall between two courtyards. It tells us what happens to food sitting on top of that wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The top of the wall is open to both courtyards, and each side can reach it equally. So both sides may use it right there by eating on top. Bringing the food down into one courtyard counts as carrying from that shared spot into a courtyard, and that is forbidden when the two courtyards made separate עירובין.

keyTerms.meaning: On its top (the top of the wall)

steps.confusionAlert: Eating is allowed, but moving the food down is not. The rule restricts carrying the food off the wall. It does not restrict using the food.

phrases.english: If there was produce on its top —
these go up from here and eat,
and those go up from there and eat,
provided that they do not bring it down below.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case of the 10-by-4 wall from step 16 and adds the rule for produce resting on top of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both courtyards may climb and eat produce on top of the wall, but may not lower it into a courtyard.

steps.title: A breach in the wall: up to ten אמות versus more
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a gap of up to ten אמות counts as a doorway, so the courtyards may make two עירובין or one. A wider gap forces a single עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the wall was broken open, up to ten אמות, they make two עירובין, and if they want they may make one, because the gap is like a doorway. If the gap is more than that, they make one עירוב and may not make two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now changes the case to a wall with a hole broken through it. It explains how the size of the hole affects the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of ten אמות or less is treated like a normal doorway (פתח). The wall still separates the courtyards, but there is also a way through, so they may stay separate or join. A gap wider than ten אמות cancels the wall as a divider, so the two courtyards become one domain and must make one עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten cubits, the maximum width of a doorway

steps.whatToRemember: Ten אמות is the dividing line. Up to ten counts as a doorway, so there is a choice of one or two עירובין. More than ten erases the wall, so only one עירוב is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ten-אמות limit for a פתח is a basic measure that appears again and again in the laws of partitions on שבת.

phrases.english: If the wall was breached,
up to ten cubits —
they make two eiruvin,
and if they wish, they make one,
because it is like a doorway.
More than this —
they make one eiruv and do not make two.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִפְרְצָה הַכּוֹתֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the case from an intact wall to a breached wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A breach of up to ten אמות counts as a doorway, so one or two עירובין may be made. A breach of more than ten אמות requires a single עירוב.

steps.title: What if the wall is less than four טפחים wide?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the law is for a wall that is less than four טפחים wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If the wall does not have four טפחים of width, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a question the משנה did not answer. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only discussed a wall four טפחים wide, which is wide enough to count as a space of its own. The question is what happens when the top of the wall is too narrow to count as its own space.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Four handbreadths, the minimum width for a space to count as its own area

phrases.english: GEMARA:
If it does not have four handbreadths, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the משנה's 4-טפחים wall and asks about a narrower one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for a dividing wall whose top is less than four טפחים wide.

steps.title: רב: both domains control it, so nothing may be moved there
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the air of both courtyards controls the narrow wall-top, so one may not move anything on it, not even a hair's breadth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The air of two domains controls it, so one may not move anything on it, even as much as a hair's width.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question from step 19. A narrow wall-top is treated as belonging to both courtyards at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall four טפחים wide counts as its own space, so both sides may use it. A narrower wall-top is just part of both courtyards, and each courtyard's domain reaches over it. Because the two courtyards did not join with one עירוב, the overlap makes the spot forbidden to both, so nothing may be shifted there even slightly.
steps.confusionAlert: You might expect a narrower wall to be easier to use than a wide one. It is actually stricter. A wide wall is its own space that both sides can share, while a narrow one belongs to both courtyards and so is forbidden to both.
steps.whatToRemember: Wall four טפחים wide: both sides may eat on top but not bring the food down. Wall less than four טפחים: two domains control it, so nothing may be moved on it at all.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The air of two domains controls it,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יָזִיז בּוֹ אֲפִילּוּ מְלֹא נִימָא.
phrases.english: one may not move anything on it, even a hair's breadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אֲוִיר שְׁתֵּי רְשׁוּיוֹת שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A wall less than four טפחים wide is controlled by both courtyards, so nothing may be moved on it at all.
